newsitem.title: USA: USDA's Drazek hopeful on EU vet pact by month end.
newsitem.headline: USDA's Drazek hopeful on EU vet pact by month end.

text.p: U.S. Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman's trade adviser Paul Drazek Tuesday said he was hopeful an agreement could be reached with the European Union on veterinary standards by the end of the month.
"We're making headway," Drazek told Reuters. "We're hopeful we'll reach an agreement by the end of February."

U.S. and EU officials have been meeting in Washington on the issue as precursor to talks in Brussels later this month. An EU source said the meetings had been going for two full days and that "the atmosphere was good."
In December, the two sides agreed to extend current arrangements to April to allow time for the talks to be concluded.

Washington has been concerned that an estimated $2.0 billion in trade in veterinary and phytosanitary products could be disrupted as the EU harmonises import rules in the 15 member states, resulting in stricter standards.
An EU official said on Jan. 20 the talks were progressing and might be resolved by late February.
